The edge of a large monsoon surge is expected to bring scattered
showers and isolated thunderstorms later tonight through tomorrow. 
By Sunday night, 92W looks to shift slightly closer, causing a 
decrease in winds and sufficient moisture and instability for 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms to remain. If winds 
remain light enough and cloud cover isn't too high, the light winds 
may allow for island effect precipitation over Saipan Monday, and 
then Guam, Tinian, and Saipan Tuesday. By Wednesday, northeasterly 
winds will likely prevent further island effect as 92W moves into 
the area. As of now, most models agree that Invest 92W will move 
through as only a weak disturbance, or possibly a tropical 
depression, with only the GFS deterministic model showing a stronger 
system. Therefore, it looks like a wetter pattern is in store for the
Marianas by the end of next week. Invest 92W will continue to be 
monitored closely for any changes to expected development. 

Marine...
Gentle to moderate southwesterlies prevail across the Marianas 
and will persist through the Sunday, before decreasing to light to
gentle Sunday night. Combined seas of 5 to 7 feet are now expected
to remain fairly steady, possibly increasing slightly Sunday
night. Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms are expected
through the entire forecast period, with a wetter pattern possible
beginning Tuesday depending on the development and track of a 
tropical disturbance in eastern Micronesia, well to the southeast.

Tropical Systems...
A broad, weak circulation, Invest 92W, sits in an elongated
surface trough and is centered north of Pohnpei near 10N156E, moving
west-northwest. 92W remains sub-low, meaning no development is 
expected over the next couple of days. Numerous heavy showers and 
isolated thunderstorms are found to the west of the center, where 
the strongest convergence is seen, with scattered to numerous 
locally heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms found in a band to 
the south of the trough and Invest 92W where southerly winds are 
crossing the Equator and converging with the monsoonal flow over 
Micronesia. Invest 92W is expected to move west-northwest, then turn
more northwest over the next couple of days with little to no change
in intensity. The trough looks to strengthen a bit over the next few
days, possibly becoming the main monsoon trough over the next week.

Invest 93W is seen to the north-northwest of the far northern CNMI 
near 24N145E, moving quickly northeast. The invest lies within the 
weakening monsoon trough. 93W was dropped from high to medium 
yesterday, then back to sub-low overnight as it loses its momentum, 
definitely showing signs of weakening. Invest 93W will continue to 
move northeast, likely moving north of 25N this evening.

Eastern Micronesia...
Invest 92W, along with the trough that 92W is embedded in, remains 
active across eastern Micronesia, producing scattered to numerous
across the Marshall Islands with scattered showers and isolated
thunderstorms currently over Kosrae. Pohnpei is seeing only isolated
showers at this time. Convection across Pohnpei looks to increase
later this evening as 92W progresses northwest, with convection
increasing at Kosrae Sunday morning. Strong convergence to the south
of the trough and 92W will drift north as 92W moves northwest then
north over the next couple of days. The strong band of showers
currently seen to the south of both locations is being produced along
a monsoon surge that is interacting with a band of convergence
produced by south winds crossing the Equator and converging with the
monsoonal winds to the south of Pohnpei and Kosrae. For majuro,
showers look to clear out later this evening, however, this will be
short-lived as the trough meanders over the Marshalls and becomes
active again by Sunday morning. Overall, a very wet and active
pattern looks to continue for a few days over the region. As 92W
moves out of the area next week, a drier pattern will move into
eastern Micronesia.

Southerly swell emanating from a broad circulation to the distant 
south, near the Solomon Islands, is producing a south to southwest
swell high enough to generate hazardous surf of 6 to 9 feet along 
south-facing reefs of Kosrae. Therefore, a High Surf Advisory will
remain in effect for Kosrae through Tuesday afternoon. For Pohnpei
and Majuro, surf will remain below hazardous levels. Gentle to fresh
winds are expected for Pohnpei and Kosrae through the middle of next
week, while Majuro sees light to gentle winds. Fresh to near gale 
gusts are possible with heavier showers into the beginning of next
week.

Western Micronesia...
Satellite observations show mostly clear to partly cloudy skies 
across Palau and Yap, and mostly cloudy skies across Chuuk. 
Altimetry shows combined seas between 3 and 5 feet across Palau and 
Yap, and 7 to 10 feet across Chuuk.
